title: 8-round AES-256: reported whole-key herd partial sums

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 8-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-8r-integral-fklssww2001-herd-near-codebook-cp; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Selected near-codebook of 2^128-2^119 distinct plaintexts, forming about 2^23 undamaged herds of 2^104 texts.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.
About 26 herds isolate the tested subkey material; the first four dominate the stated running time.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.note: The source estimates 2^202 work per dominating herd and four dominating herds, for 2^204 trial-encryption equivalents; about 26 herds are checked in total. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: The near-codebook is acquired once. Testing multiple herds does not mean re-acquiring this codebook once per herd. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.note: Section 2.6 explicitly gives this storage for the eight-round herd/partial-sum construction.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: The exact key_recovery endpoint has no numerical joint success. The zero sum over the entire unpartitioned codebook also holds for wrong guesses and is not a distinguisher; the attack uses correctly partitioned complete herds. The near-codebook construction leaves about half of the herds undamaged, a coverage count rather than a random-selection success rate. The source discusses about26 herd checks for a unique candidate and different AES192/256 schedule costs, without a quantified wrong-key distribution or full-output probability. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6–9 Sections2.5–2.6: within a complete herd formed using the correct initial key hypothesis, the targeted byte of b5 sums to zero. For near-codebook data this is conditional on selecting an undamaged herd; it is not a claim about randomly choosing one.
